items.title: "Aktualisierungsgebühr" payment demanded
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date, not a period to be counted. "zahlbar bis 30.11.2026" is given explicitly. 2026-11-30 is a Monday, not a weekend day or a public holiday in NRW, so no §193 BGB shift is needed. Due date as stated: 2026-11-30.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a scam/phishing demand rather than a genuine German authority letter: there is no official government body called "Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland" responsible for vehicle registration — that is handled by the local Kfz-Zulassungsstelle/Straßenverkehrsamt, not by a private postal-box sender in Berlin.

The payment is to be sent to a Lithuanian IBAN (LT98...) to an individual named 'R. Kazlauskas', not to a German public-authority account and not to an account matching the sender's name — this is a classic scam pattern (foreign IBAN, private payee, for an alleged state fee).

The letter uses pressure/urgency tactics (threat that the vehicle registration 'may be suspended' from January 2027, and threat to report to the 'Zulassungsstelle') typical of fake-invoice scams targeting vehicle owners.

There is no Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung (legal remedy instructions) and no real legal basis or statutory reference for this 'Aktualisierungsgebühr', which a genuine official fee notice would normally include.

Recommendation: do not pay this invoice; verify directly with your local Zulassungsstelle/Straßenverkehrsamt whether any update to your vehicle registration is actually required, and consider reporting this letter as a potential scam/fraud attempt.
